checks.check: the relay under test is the one inside the shipped image
the relay starts and listens (accept() succeeds)
`nc 127.0.0.1 <port>` returns a dump and exits 0 (the relay closes)
the dump says what it is: READ-ONLY, and how to reconnect
checks.detail: # nx679j v9 DIAGNOSTIC RELAY - READ-ONLY SNAPSHOT

checks.check: all ten sections are present, in order
the dump is readable text (printable ASCII + \n/\t only)
the journal section carries the real journal, line by line
the journal hashes in the dump are the hashes of the file on disk
the relay reports the address the kernel really bound and shows it is present on an interface here
checks.detail: [relay] version=nx679j-relay-v9 port=40833 bind=127.0.0.1 bind_all=0 listen_ok=1 | [relay] wanted_ip=127.0.0.1 on_an_interface=yes(lo) nonlocal_bind=-

checks.check: client 1 (prefix 0 bytes) is served completely
client 2 (prefix 25 bytes) is served completely
client 3 (prefix 10 bytes) is served completely
what the client SENDS changes nothing: sections [1]..[8] are the same for all three clients (only live /proc counters may differ)
the SHIPPED relay announces its own 30 s client deadline
checks.detail: [relay] client_deadline_s=30 file_cap=65536 journal_window=524288 (one client is killed on that deadline, so a reader that stops reading cannot hold the relay)

checks.check: the deadline is configurable for tests (V9_RELAY_DEADLINE=5 here)
checks.detail: [relay] client_deadline_s=5 file_cap=65536 journal_window=524288 (one client is killed on that deadline, so a reader that stops reading cannot hold the relay)

checks.check: another client is served while the rude one is still hanging
after the deadline the rude client is gone: the relay reports no leftover serving child
with no argument the shipped relay listens on 9999 and says so in the dump (this is the port the phone uses)
nothing in the device tree was touched by any of it
checks.detail: 30 files hashed before and after, 0 differences

checks.check: a 2.8 MB journal still yields a bounded dump whose hashes are exact
the window is the NEWEST complete lines of the journal, and says so

checks.check: the dump grew by less than the journal did (it is a window, not a copy)
no file is ever opened for writing
no syscall that mutates the device is executed at all
checks.detail: 32 distinct syscalls, none of them a write to the system

checks.check: the network is only READ, never configured (no SIOCSIFADDR)
checks.detail: 28 ioctl calls, SIOCGIFADDR present, SIOCSIFADDR absent

checks.check: every write goes to the console (fd 1/2) or to a socket: nothing is ever written to a file, a device or the rawdump
the relay really served both clients in the traced run
